option_description: The attacker capability this path needs, on a three-step scale from the lowest to the highest: opportunistic, targeted, advanced. The hidden-edges module sets it from the edge-kind table's default for the table row that found the path. When several rows found the same path, only the rows at the path's tier count, and of those it takes the row that is easiest for the attacker; a lower-tier row's defaults never apply. The operator may change it in Dethereal's review before accepting the edge.
security_impact: The class policy does not read it. It tells an analysis which attackers can take this path: the lower the capability, the more attackers can. Table defaults for this kind: opportunistic for Remote Services (T1021) paths; targeted for Exploitation of Remote Services (T1210) paths.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the candidate's "base" values in the hidden-edge review table. To change the value before accepting, reply "edit <n> capability: <value>". There is nothing to discover from code or configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: base.required_capability is one of: opportunistic, targeted, advanced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: After the accept, read required_capability in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: The privilege the attacker must already hold at the source end to take this path. none: no account. user: an ordinary account. admin: an administrator account. system: the highest privilege on the host. The hidden-edges module sets it from the edge-kind table's default for the row that found the path; the operator may change it in Dethereal's review.
security_impact: The class policy does not read it. It tells an analysis what the attacker must have won at the source before this path opens. Table default for this kind: user, for every path.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the candidate's "base" values in the hidden-edge review table. To change the value before accepting, reply "edit <n> required: <value>". There is nothing to discover from code or configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: base.required_privilege is one of: none, user, admin, system.

how_to_obtain.instruction: After the accept, read required_privilege in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: The privilege the attacker holds at the target end once the path is taken: none, user, admin or system. The hidden-edges module sets it from the edge-kind table's default for the row that found the path; the operator may change it in Dethereal's review.
security_impact: The class policy reads it to set the criticality and score of each of this flow's Inferred Path exposures (none: low, 3.0; user: medium, 5.0; admin: high, 7.5; system: critical, 9.0; missing or invalid: medium, 5.0), and states it at the end of each exposure's description ("grants <value> at the target"; "unstated" when missing or invalid). It also tells an analysis what the attacker gains at the target, and so what the next step of an attack path can start from. Table defaults for this kind: user; admin for a login on a host over RDP or SSH (T1021.001, T1021.004), and for a path that starts from an Administrator.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the candidate's "base" values in the hidden-edge review table. To change the value before accepting, reply "edit <n> granted: <value>". There is nothing to discover from code or configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: base.granted_privilege is one of: none, user, admin, system.

how_to_obtain.instruction: After the accept, read granted_privilege in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: The kind of inferred path this flow records: remote-service. Fixed and read-only. A flow of this class is an inferred attack path that an operator accepted in Dethereal after review. It is not a declared flow, and it is never the class of an ordinary data flow. It says that an attacker who holds the source component can reach a remote service on the target component over the network, although the model declares no flow between them. The attacker logs in to the service with a valid account (Remote Services, T1021), or exploits it (Exploitation of Remote Services, T1210). They gain the logged-on account's rights at the target, or the exploited service's rights.
security_impact: The class policy reads it to name this flow's Inferred Path exposures ("Inferred remote service path: <id>") and to set their attack vector: NETWORK for this kind. For an analysis, the flow is a step an attacker may take from the source to the target, not traffic the system sends.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Dethereal writes the kind from the accepted candidate (the "kind" column of the hidden-edge review table). There is nothing to discover from code or configuration. Never give this class to an ordinary flow.
After the accept, read hidden_edge_kind in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: The ATT&CK techniques an attacker uses at the target end to take this path. Dethereal writes them from the accepted candidate; the review cannot edit them, and they are read-only on the platform. For this kind: T1021 Remote Services; T1021.001 Remote Desktop Protocol or T1021.004 SSH, when the host's own exposure names them; T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services. When several findings support one path, it carries only the techniques of the findings at the path's tier: a lower-tier finding's technique never rides on a higher-tier path. The path is inferred from the model's exposures, their ATT&CK techniques and the model's structure, and an operator reviewed it. It is not a declared flow.
security_impact: Each id becomes one exposure of this flow in category Inferred Path, named "Inferred remote service path: <id>" (for example "Inferred remote service path: T1021"), exploited by that technique, with attack vector NETWORK. Its description ends with "Confidence: <tier>; grants <granted_privilege> at the target." Its criticality and score come from granted_privilege only, never from the tier (none: low, 3.0; user: medium, 5.0; admin: high, 7.5; system: critical, 9.0; missing or invalid: medium, 5.0). The policy reads only the first 10 entries, and only well-formed ATT&CK ids (T1234 or T1234.567) count. The category lets a consumer tell these findings apart from findings on declared elements. Breakers: when an attribute or control below holds in the model, the hidden-edges module stops proposing this path ("removes") or proposes it at a lower tier ("lowers"). An edge already accepted stays in the model until its flow is removed; Dethereal then records it as rejected, so it is not proposed again. Removes: east_west_within_segment_restricted true on the Network Segment above the target, or on the Network Segment the source exposure is on. Removes: east_west_microsegmentation_enforced true on the Application Layer that holds both ends, on the Application Layer the source exposure is on, or on the Internal Service Communication flow the source exposure is on. Removes, for paths found from a Network Segment, Management & Monitoring Plane, Operating System / Host or Application Layer exposure, from a Secure Remote Access or Internal Service Communication flow, or from an exploitable service on a component: a Firewall Policy control with east_west_microsegmentation_enforced true, attached to the target or a boundary above it. Removes: vpn_pool_to_trust_segmentation_enforced true on the VPN Gateway the path starts from. Removes: user_segment_isolated_from_production_tiers true on the Endpoint / Office Environment the path starts from, or a Network Access Control control with that attribute true attached to it. Lowers: east_west_microsegmentation_enforced true on the Application Layer above the target. Lowers: remote_admin_access_hardened true on the Operating System / Host above the target. Lowers: control_plane_access_mediated_by_pam_with_recording true on the Management & Monitoring Plane the source exposure is on. Lowers, for paths found from a Network Segment or Management & Monitoring Plane exposure, a Secure Remote Access flow, or a host's RDP or SSH exposure: a Privileged Access Management control with privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_recording or bastion_mediates_all_admin_access true, or a Multi-Factor Authentication control with mfa_enforced_for_admin true, attached to the target or a boundary above it. Paths from a VPN Gateway, an Administrator or an Endpoint / Office Environment have no Firewall Policy, Privileged Access Management or Multi-Factor Authentication breaker. Lowers: least_privilege_access_enforced true on the VPN Gateway the path starts from. Lowers: no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_required, least_privilege_admin_scoping or privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_recording true on the Administrator the path starts from. Lowers: admin_protocols_require_pam_and_mfa true on the Endpoint / Office Environment the path starts from; segment_boundary_enforced or inter_segment_traffic_filtered_by_identity true on the Network Segment above the target. Strengthens: permit_any_from_vpn_pool true on the VPN Gateway the path starts from raises the tier one step.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the "techniques" column of the candidate in the hidden-edge review table. There is nothing to discover from code or configuration.
After the accept, read technique_ids in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: The ids of the exposures the path was inferred from. Dethereal writes them from the accepted candidate, and they are read-only on the platform; at most 50 are kept. When several findings support one path, only the exposures of those at the path's tier are listed. For this kind they are exposures on a Network Segment, Management & Monitoring Plane, Operating System / Host, Application Layer or Endpoint / Office Environment boundary; on a Secure Remote Access or Internal Service Communication flow, whose responder is the target; on a Cache / In-Memory Store, Email Server, File Storage / Shared Volume, Monitoring Agent or User Workstation / Endpoint component, which is the target; or on a VPN Gateway or Administrator, which is the source. A path from a Network Segment, Management & Monitoring Plane or Application Layer exposure also lists the target's own confirmed exposure, when it has one.
security_impact: The class policy does not read it. The ids tie the edge to its evidence: when an exposure listed here is fixed or disposed, the path loses its ground. When the operator accepts this edge on its own, not through accept-all, Dethereal marks each pending exposure listed here as affirmed on the platform. When the flow is later removed, Dethereal lists the affirmed exposures it cites for triage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the "exposures" column of the candidate in the hidden-edge review table; it shows the exposures by name. There is nothing to discover from code or configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more exposure names, each on an element of the model.

how_to_obtain.instruction: After the accept, read source_exposure_ids in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: Who shaped the accepted edge. rule: accepted as the hidden-edges module proposed it; operator: the operator edited it before accepting, by changing a base value or a kind field, or by adding a rationale. Adding only a rationale also makes it operator, while the values on the flow may still be the module's. Dethereal writes it from the accepted candidate; it is read-only on the platform.
security_impact: The class policy does not read it. rule means the values on the flow are the module's. operator means the operator edited the candidate: the values may be the operator's, or still the module's when only a rationale was added. An edited candidate is never accepted through accept-all; each one needs its own accept.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether the operator edited the candidate in the hidden-edge review: any edit of capability, required, granted, a kind field or the rationale makes it operator. There is nothing to discover from code or configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: rule for an unedited accept; operator after any edit.

how_to_obtain.instruction: After the accept, read proposed_by in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: How firmly the model's facts support the path, as the hidden-edges module rated it. high: the exposure the path rests on is confirmed, and the attributes that would break the path are stated false. medium: only one of the two holds, or a breaker lowered the path. low: neither holds, or the path is capped at low. Each attribute or control that weakens the path lowers it one step. A pending exposure caps it at medium. When several findings support one path, the highest tier counts, and the path keeps only the techniques, exposures and base values of the findings at that tier. When the optional knowledge-graph check runs, it can lower the tier one step, never raise it. Dethereal writes the tier from the accepted candidate; the review cannot edit it, and it is read-only on the platform.
security_impact: The class policy states the tier in each Inferred Path exposure's description ("Confidence: <tier>"); a missing or unknown tier is stated as low. The tier does not set the exposure's criticality or score: those come from granted_privilege. The table caps this kind at high for paths found from a Network Segment or Management & Monitoring Plane, a Secure Remote Access flow, a host's RDP or SSH exposure, or an exploitable service on a component. It caps them at medium when they are found from an Internal Service Communication flow, an Application Layer, a VPN Gateway, an Administrator or an Endpoint / Office Environment. High needs these attributes stated false, not left empty: east_west_within_segment_restricted, east_west_microsegmentation_enforced, and remote_admin_access_hardened (on the host the source exposure is on), wherever they apply. A path found from a Network Segment or Management & Monitoring Plane exposure reaches high only when the target has its own confirmed exposure of the same technique family.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the "tier" column of the candidate in the hidden-edge review table. "kg": "lowered" beside it means the knowledge-graph check lowered it. There is nothing to discover from code or configuration.
After the accept, read tier in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.

option_description: The operator's own words on why the path holds, at most 1000 characters. The operator gives it in Dethereal's review before accepting. Empty unless the operator wrote one.
security_impact: The class policy does not read it. It records the operator's reasoning for later reviewers. Adding one counts as an edit: proposed_by becomes operator, and the candidate leaves accept-all.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the hidden-edge review, reply "edit <n> rationale: <text>" before accepting the candidate. Write why the path holds in this system.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The candidate shows the rationale and is marked as edited.

how_to_obtain.instruction: After the accept, read rationale in the flow's attribute file in the Dethereal model directory, under "attributes". A new hidden-edge flow's id is "he-" followed by 16 hex characters.
